## Data access API

Each generated repository implements `IRepository<TEntity, TKey>`. The main methods are as follows.

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `GetByIdAsync(id, ct)` | Gets a single entity by primary key (null when not found). |
| `GetAllAsync(ct)` | Gets all entities. |
| `InsertAsync(entity, ct)` | Inserts a single entity. |
| `UpdateAsync(entity, mode, ct)` | Updates the single entity matching the primary key (returns whether it succeeded). `mode` selects the concurrency policy for tables that have a rowversion column. |
| `DeleteAsync(id, ct)` | Deletes the single entity matching the primary key (returns whether it succeeded). The delete is unconditional: a key carries no rowversion, so nothing is compared. To delete under the protection of the version you read, use `MarkRemoved()` + `SaveAsync`. |
| `SaveAsync(entity, cascadeSave, cascadeDelete, insertWhenUpdateMissing, mode, ct)` | Saves one aggregate root's inserts, updates, and deletes in a single transaction according to RowState (children cascade by default; returns the number of records saved). `mode` selects the concurrency policy, and the save hooks (`ISaveHook<T>`) fire here. |
| `SaveAsync(entities, cascadeSave, cascadeDelete, insertWhenUpdateMissing, mode, ct)` | Saves multiple aggregate roots together in one transaction (all succeed or all roll back), otherwise identical to the single-root form. |
| `BulkInsertAsync(entities, ct)` | Inserts multiple entities at once (returns the number inserted). |
| `Query()` | Builds queries such as filtering, ordering, and row limiting. |
| `CheckUniquenessAsync(entity, ct)` | Checks this table's UNIQUE constraints against the database and returns the violations (rows sharing the primary key are excluded, so the same call fits insert and update). |

The uniqueness check is advisory: the definitive guarantee is the database's own UNIQUE constraint. When edit models are generated, `EditModelCollection<T>.Validate()` also flags duplicates among the elements themselves, and `{EditModel}.ValidateUniqueAsync(repository)` registers the database-side violations on the binding properties.

For the supported scope and details of `Query()`, see [docs/code-generation.md](https://github.com/kokko-labs/QuickER/blob/main/docs/code-generation.md).

Two generated extensions ride on `Query()`: `IncludeGraph()` includes the same child-direction cascade a graph save walks (combine it with `Where` or `GetByIdAsync` to bound what is fetched), and `GetByIdAsync(id)` fetches a single entity by key at the end of a query chain — `Query().IncludeGraph().GetByIdAsync(id)` reads one aggregate together with its whole graph.

## Usage

### DI registration

Registers the QuickER Repository (Sqlite) with the DI container.

```csharp
services.AddGeneratedSqliteRepositories(connectionString);
```

### CRUD and queries

Using `CustomerEntity` (primary key type `int`) as an example, here are the representative operations.

```csharp
// Insert
var entity = new CustomerEntity();
await repository.InsertAsync(entity);

// Get by primary key
var found = await repository.GetByIdAsync(1);

// Get all
var all = await repository.GetAllAsync();

// Query (filter / order)
var results = await repository
    .Query()
    .OrderBy(x => x.CustomerId)
    .ToListAsync();

// Update / delete
if (found is not null)
{
    await repository.UpdateAsync(found);
    await repository.DeleteAsync(1);
}
```
